findings.description: setRatio uses `if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert RatioTooHigh()` but the documented invariant (lines 29-30, 91) is that ratio must be STRICTLY less than MAX_RATIO (50) — 'Max settable ratio is MAX_RATIO - 1'. The operator should be `>=`. As written, a ratio of exactly 50 is accepted, and DEFAULT_RATIO is already 50, so the constructor itself sets ratio to a value the spec says is out of range. Contradicts the contract's own stated bound; the off-by-one means the realised mint-debt is 50% of dispatched USDS rather than the intended <50% cap.
missingMitigations: Operator does not enforce the documented strict-less-than bound; should be `newRatio >= MAX_RATIO`
findings.notes: ratio setter is onlyOwner, but this is a spec-vs-code boundary deviation (the bound itself is wrong), not an owner-attack. Manual review should confirm intended semantics of MAX_RATIO vs DEFAULT_RATIO.

findings.description: migrate() runs an outer loop over [1, v1.nextIndex()) and, for each index the caller holds, an inner loop `for (j = 0; j < balance; j++)` that calls v2.mintFor(...) once per NFT held. Total external calls scale with the caller's entire V1 NFT balance across all indexes. A user (or a holder who was airdropped/accumulated many V1 NFTs) with a large aggregate balance cannot migrate in a single transaction once the cost exceeds the block gas limit, permanently blocking their migration (migrate() has no pagination or partial-migration path). Self-inflicted for most users, but balances are not user-controllable downward (no partial migrate), so a sufficiently large holder is bricked.
missingMitigations: No pagination / per-index or bounded-quantity migrate variant
mintFor is called once per NFT instead of batch-minting `balance` in one _mint call
findings.notes: v1.nextIndex() is owner-bounded (small), but `balance` is unbounded per holder. Also note setMappings (line 43) and setInitialized (line 53) loop over nextIndex but are owner-only and bounded.

findings.description: onDispatch computes `added = (amount * ratio) / 100`. Multiplication-before-division is correct ordering, but integer division truncates: for small dispatched `amount` (or low ratio) `added` rounds to 0 and the code early-returns (line 119), so that dispatch accrues no mint-debt. Repeated small dispatches systematically under-accrue the phUSD debt ledger vs the nominal ratio%. Value-leak is bounded by the per-dispatch rounding remainder.
missingMitigations: No remainder carry-forward; truncated dust is silently dropped
findings.notes: Low impact; flagged for completeness. Related to (but distinct from) the documented basis-point price-compounding known issue, which is excluded.

findings.description: unlockCallback sizes the donation/LP split off `balanceOf(address(this))` snapshotted in pool() (line 192) and the donation swap (line 226) executes against live Balancer V3 pool reserves. The swap path passes limitRaw: 0 (line 223) and relies solely on the post-unwrap USDC slippage check (`usdcReceived >= minUSDC`, line 235) supplied by the authorized pooler. If a pooler passes a low/zero minUSDC, an in-block reserve manipulation (sandwich) of the sUSDS->waUSDC swap could extract value on the donation leg. Mitigated in practice by: pool() being onlyAuthorizedPooler + nonReentrant + whenNotPaused, and the caller-supplied minUSDC/minBPT floors.
missingMitigations: limitRaw set to 0 on the intermediate swap; slippage protection delegated entirely to the pooler-supplied minUSDC, no on-chain TWAP/oracle reference
findings.notes: Requires a careless or compromised authorized pooler to set minUSDC too low; pooler trust + slippage params reduce severity. Donation phase is the newly-added Story-031 code path. Worth manual review of the minUSDC sizing guidance for poolers.
